messages:
maria: Quick thread — we need a succinct checklist for the load experiments before we publish any claims. replay harness vs synthetic generator keeps coming up.
kevin: +1. From infra side: replay == real request shapes but hides sequence-tail warmup effects. synthetic lets us stress specific kernels.
anya: Can we agree on canonical metric defs first? I keep seeing TTFT/TPOT ambiguity in writeups.
sam: Proposal: TTFT = server-side time from request accepted to first token emitted (includes scheduling, kernel init, KV restore). TPOT = time to produce the remainder of payload per-token (steady-state tail) measured for a fixed N tokens. Both measured at p50/p95/p99.
maria: Sounds good. Add QPS vs goodput note: QPS is accepted requests/sec, goodput is finished tokens/sec that contributed to useful output (i.e., excludes short-circuited errors and cached-fast hits?).
kevin: Important: with KV cache hits, TTFT can be artificially low because prefix work is skipped. We should report runs with cold KV, warm KV, and realistic hybrid ratios.
anya: Agreed. Suggest three profiles: cold-start (empty KV, synthetic long prefixes), warm (full KV warmup), and replay (actual traffic with distribution). Label them clearly in plots.
perf-bot: reminder: previous run 1738899000 had kernel swap causing +18% p95. See logs: ```kernel_select: fallback->int8_quantized
p95: baseline 98ms -> 116ms
trace_id: zyx-334
``` 
sam: That regression got fixed by pinning a smaller-intro kernel for short sequences, but it exposed our batching heuristic mismatch (we were mixing sequence-length buckets incorrectly).
maria: Can you paste the batching rule change we landed? I want it in the checklist.
kevin: Patch is tiny: ```if seq_len < 64: prefer kernelA, else prefer kernelB; if batch mix ratio > 0.6 long: cap short-batch size to 16``` — rationale: long sequences dominate kv memory and stall small kernel lanes.
anya: We should also include profiler artifacts requirement: for each benchmark upload flamegraph, kernel selection trace, batch composition histogram, and KV hit-rate timeline. Without them reviewers can't reproduce cause.
sam: One more: tests must run with fixed CPU/gpu visibility env and no autoscaler changes. i.e., `export NODE_SCALE=0` in harness. Otherwise scheduling noise kills p99 comparability.
maria: Nice. Last ask: add a one-paragraph explanation in the top of each bench doc describing why we prefer replay for apples-to-apples latency claims but synthetic for isolating kernel behaviour.
kevin: I'll draft that and include an example table: cold/warm/replay rows with columns: TTFT_p50,p95,p99; TPOT_token_ms_avg; QPS; goodput.
anya: Great — once kevin posts the draft, can someone run a sanity run and attach profiler for next-week doc review?
sam: I'll kick one off after lunch and tag results here.
perf-bot: run-scheduled: 1738902000 triggered by @sam — will post artifacts when complete. :robot_face:
thread_summary: Bench checklist: define TTFT/TPOT, include cold/warm/replay profiles, report KV hit modes, attach profiler artifacts, note batching/kernel rules and env controls
